name: call_target_four_times
description: Calls one target routine four times in a row with no arguments and then returns. Its only work is delegating to that target.

name: update_countdown_and_step_index
description: Calls one routine first, then counts down a byte timer in a record. When the timer reaches zero it reloads it and moves a 16-bit index up toward 63 or down toward zero, depending on a direction flag, and copies the new index to a second record.

name: copy_or_default_pair_out
description: When a flag byte in the record is clear, copies a stored long value and a count word to the output record if the count is nonzero. Otherwise it writes a supplied default value with a count of one.

name: call_target_four_times
description: Calls one target routine four times in a row with no arguments and then returns. Its only work is delegating to that target.

name: advance_animation_frame_entry
description: If a flag byte is set, it stores the incoming word and loads a new frame record from a table, indexed by a counter, into the current record, then clears the flag. It returns the low byte of its input rotated left by one bit.

name: call_target_four_times
description: Calls one target routine four times in a row with no arguments and then returns. Its only work is delegating to that target.

name: dispatch_via_jump_table_entry
description: Reads a selector byte from a record, clears it, and uses a second byte as an index into a table of offsets to call the matching handler. The table is addressed relative to the routine itself.

name: empty_stub_routine
description: Does nothing and returns immediately, so it is an empty stub with no body.

name: set_global_flag_bit_one
description: Sets the second-lowest bit of a shared global variable and returns. Nothing else is changed.

name: set_global_flag_bit_one
description: Sets the second-lowest bit of a shared global variable and returns. The reference data lists hardware registers for this routine, but the decompiled body only sets that bit, so no hardware access is visible in this listing.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler could only decode bad instruction data here, so the routine body is not recovered and no behaviour can be stated from this listing. It is referenced only as a handler pointer stored in data.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Decoding stopped at bad instruction data, so this block is not recovered in the listing. Only its size and its use as a handler pointer are known.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Decoding stopped at bad instruction data, so this block is not recovered in the listing. Only its size and its use as a handler pointer are known.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Decoding stopped at bad instruction data, so this block is not recovered in the listing. Only its size and its use as a handler pointer are known.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Decoding stopped at bad instruction data, so this block is not recovered in the listing. Only its size and its use as a handler pointer are known.

name: unpack_rnc_block_list
description: Walks a linked list of memory blocks looking for one tagged as RNC-compressed, then decodes it with literal copies and back-references into newly allocated memory. It then calls a function through a global library pointer to finish.

name: extract_flag_bit_from_table
description: Scans a table of word pairs until a masked global value matches the second word of a pair. It reads a shift count from the matched entry, compares it with a stored byte, and may call another routine before returning a masked value with one more bit set.

name: mask_and_conditional_call
description: Ands a word with a mask word, and if a byte value is less than another byte it calls another routine and returns that routine's result instead of the masked word.

name: return_empty_routine
description: Contains no operations and returns immediately, so calls to it have no effect.

name: build_bit_length_tables
description: Reads a count and fills a byte buffer on the stack with values from a source routine. It then builds per-level tables of bit masks, shifted values and derived masks for each of seventeen bit-length levels, based on a key list.

name: process_pending_entry_chain
description: When a header value matches a fixed marker, it walks a chain of pending entries, clears them, and writes a computed offset into a table slot for each entry. Its references include exec.FreeMem.

name: return_empty_routine
description: Contains no operations and returns immediately, so calls to it have no effect.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: If a buffer pointer is supplied, copies sixteen 32-bit values from a fixed table in the data area into it. It then calls a second routine through a stored pointer.

name: initialize_program_entry
description: Runs a series of setup calls, including a call through a stored function pointer and a second call through a global table pointer. It clears a longword through a pointer and returns the two data registers as its result.

name: initialize_program_entry
description: Runs a series of setup calls, including a call through a stored function pointer and a second call through a global table pointer. It clears a longword through a pointer and returns the two data registers as its result.

name: decode_compressed_bitstream_blocks
description: Decodes compressed data in blocks by reading bits, copying literal bytes or back-referenced runs into an output buffer, and then updating a table of word counts. It relies on helper routines for bit shifting, table lookup and table filling.

name: run_command_in_background
description: Parses the command line for an optional stack size switch and the command to run, then opens the DOS library and starts the command as a background task with redirected input and output. It reports an error for an invalid parameter and rejects a stack size below a minimum.

name: measure_string_and_call_library
description: Scans a null-terminated string to find its length, then calls two library functions in sequence with it. The referenced text is the start of a "Can't find" message, so it appears to report a failed lookup.

name: initialize_program_entry
description: Runs a series of setup calls, including a call through a stored function pointer and a second call through a global table pointer. It clears a longword through a pointer and returns the two data registers as its result.

name: decrement_to_minus_one
description: Decrements a 16-bit register value by one repeatedly until it reaches minus one, then returns. It is a countdown loop with no other effect.

name: run_startup_library_calls
description: Writes zero through a pointer and calls a library function three times, storing each returned word into a global location. It then makes three more calls and returns zero.

name: call_three_routines_return_zero
description: Calls a FreeMem wrapper, a CloseLibrary wrapper and one more routine, then returns zero.

name: store_four_results_to_globals
description: Calls another routine four times and saves each returned value into a different slot of a data block addressed from a base register.

name: call_function_pointer
description: Calls a function pointer stored at a fixed offset from the data base. If it returns nonzero, it adds 32768 to that result; otherwise it returns zero.

name: poll_function_pointer
description: Repeatedly calls a function pointer stored in the data base until it returns nonzero. Between calls it performs a byte self-copy that has no effect.

name: call_single_routine_and_return
description: Forwards control to one other routine and returns, with no processing of its own.

name: copy_byte_buffer
description: Copies a block of bytes from a source to a destination, moving eight bytes at a time and then the remaining bytes one at a time, and writes a zero terminator after the last byte.

name: clear_globals_and_call
description: Clears one global longword, calls another routine, clears a second global longword, and returns the address of this routine.

name: repeat_call_until_flag_set
description: Repeatedly calls one routine until the zero flag condition left by that call is set. It has no other work of its own.

name: allocate_and_link_list_node
description: Allocates a memory block through a stored function pointer and, if allocation succeeds, links it at the head of a list and returns the address past its link fields. If allocation fails it raises a system trap, and the rest of that path is not recovered.

name: remove_list_node_or_allocate
description: Searches a list for a given node and, if found, unlinks it and passes it to a release routine. When the list is empty and a count is unset, it sets the count and allocates a new node to add to the list.

name: find_list_tail
description: Follows the chain of linked pointers until it reaches a null link, then stores that last node address in a global variable.

name: save_restore_global_value
description: Saves the current value of a global longword, calls two other routines, and then restores the saved value.

name: save_restore_global_value
description: Saves the current value of a global longword, calls two other routines, and then restores the saved value.

name: allocate_and_link_list_node
description: Allocates a memory block through a stored function pointer and, if allocation succeeds, links it at the head of a list and returns the address past its link fields. If allocation fails it raises a system trap, and the rest of that path is not recovered.

name: remove_list_node_or_allocate
description: Searches a list for a given node and, if found, unlinks it and passes it to a release routine. The routine also has a path that sets a count and allocates a node, which is not fully recovered in the listing.

name: find_and_unlink_list_node
description: Walks a linked list looking for a node whose next link matches a given node. If none is found and the count is unset, it allocates a node; otherwise it unlinks the matched node and calls a routine.

name: allocate_and_push_list_node
description: Allocates a memory block through a stored function pointer and, if it succeeds, pushes it onto the head of a list. If allocation fails it raises a system trap, and that path is not recovered.

name: free_all_list_nodes
description: Detaches the list head and releases it, then releases each following node in the chain through a release routine, using the exec FreeMem call.

name: stub_unimplemented_library_entry
description: Only an unimplemented-instruction marker is decoded here, so the routine body is not recovered. It is the library's entry point on disk and is referenced through a data pointer.

name: store_address_to_global
description: Saves the address passed in one address register into a global variable.

name: unlink_and_release_node
description: If a counter in the record is zero, unlinks the record from its list and releases it through the exec library FreeMem call, then returns a stored result. Otherwise it sets a flag bit in the record and returns zero.

name: set_record_flag_bit_eight
description: Sets the bit with value eight in a flag byte of the record it is given, then returns zero.

name: increment_use_count_and_init
description: If a record's flag bit with value eight is clear, increments a use counter in the record. On the first use it stores a global value and calls a library function through a fixed offset, and it returns the record address. If the bit is set it returns minus one.

name: decrement_counter_and_call
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter in a record. When the counter reaches zero and a flag bit is set, it calls another routine; when it reaches zero it also calls a library function through a fixed offset with a stored value.

name: call_single_routine_and_return
description: Forwards control to one other routine and returns, with no processing of its own.

name: convert_value_bit_by_bit
description: Converts a value held in a data register by repeatedly shifting it and comparing it against a running accumulator, building the result one bit at a time over up to 23 steps. It returns early for zero and calls another routine for negative values.

name: adjust_bitfield_value
description: Sets one bit in a working value, selected by the second input, then repeatedly doubles and subtracts to form a running difference. It stops when a count condition is met and returns the working value combined with the high word of the count.

name: call_library_and_adjust_flags
description: Calls one library routine through a fixed offset and returns its result with bit value eight cleared and bit value two set.

name: call_jump_table_entries
description: Calls a sequence of function pointers at fixed offsets from a register base, alternating between two entries with a third entry in the middle, then returns. It only dispatches calls and does no work itself.

name: handle_library_status_sequence
description: Calls library routines at fixed offsets in an order chosen by two status checks, then returns a result with some bits changed.

name: dispatch_library_status_branches
description: Calls library routines at fixed offsets in an order chosen by a sign value and two status checks, then returns a result with some bits cleared.

name: branch_library_calls_on_sign
description: Calls a library routine, then makes further library calls depending on a count and a sign value, and returns a result with some bits cleared.

name: branch_library_calls_on_count
description: Makes library calls chosen by a count and a sign value, then returns a result with some bits cleared.

name: call_library_by_sign_flag
description: Calls a library routine, then makes either two calls, one call or two other calls depending on a sign value and a flag, and returns a result with some bits cleared.

name: call_library_then_mask_result
description: Calls one library routine through a fixed offset, then calls another routine and returns its result with some bits cleared.

name: call_library_twice_then_mask
description: Calls the same library routine through a fixed offset twice, then calls another routine and returns its result with some bits cleared.

name: mask_return_value
description: Calls a function through a fixed offset twice, then calls another routine and returns its result with certain bits cleared.

name: build_value_by_shift_subtract
description: Clears the sign bit of an input value and handles a large-magnitude case with a call. It then builds a result by repeated shift and subtract steps, up to 24 of them, and calls another routine at the end when a flag is set.

name: build_value_by_shift_subtract
description: Builds a result by repeated shift and subtract steps, up to 24 of them. When the step count runs out it calls another routine, and calls a second one if a flag byte is nonzero.

name: execute_loop_with_branching
description: Runs a shift, add and subtract loop over data registers, returning once a counter runs out. On exit it calls another routine and conditionally calls a second one.

name: compute_cordic_trig_value
description: Reduces an angle by fixed multiples of pi, then runs an iterative 23-step loop of shifts, additions and table-driven subtractions to produce a trigonometric-style value. It calls other routines to finish.

name: compute_cordic_trig_value
description: Returns early when the argument is outside a range, otherwise runs the same iterative 23-step loop of shifts and table subtractions to compute a trigonometric-style value, then calls other routines to store it.

name: run_cordic_iteration_loop
description: Runs the 23-step shift and table-subtract loop used by the trigonometric code, then calls another routine to finish.

name: compute_cordic_trig_value
description: Returns early for small arguments, otherwise runs the iterative table loop to compute a trigonometric-style value, and calls other routines to store the result, depending on a sign argument.

name: run_cordic_iteration_loop
description: Runs the iterative table loop with a sign-dependent step, then calls another routine to store the result.

name: run_cordic_iteration_loop
description: Runs the iterative shift and table loop, then branches on a stored argument to call a routine and returns after a few final calls.

name: store_cordic_result_value
description: Runs a shift and table-subtract loop over one value, then calls one routine and branches to a final store path depending on a stored argument.

name: run_cordic_iteration_loop
description: Runs the iterative shift and table loop on an input value, then branches on a stored argument, storing the result through a routine call.

name: accumulate_table_steps_into_result
description: Loops over a table of words, adding or subtracting shifted values into two accumulators on each step. It then branches on a stored argument to call routines that finish the result.

description: Contains no operations and returns immediately.

name: call_single_routine_and_return
description: Calls one other routine and returns, with no other work.

name: call_two_routines_and_return
description: Calls two other routines in sequence and returns, with no other work.

name: normalize_integer_to_float
description: Converts a signed integer into a float-like form by moving it into the high word and normalising it by doubling while adjusting an exponent. Zero is left unchanged.

name: normalize_integer_to_float
description: Performs the same integer-to-float normalisation as its neighbour, but returns immediately when the high byte of the argument is minus one.

name: call_routine_then_two_more
description: Calls one routine, then calls two more in sequence, because a flag that stays clear guards them.

name: call_routine_then_three_more
description: Calls one routine, then calls three more in sequence, because a flag that stays clear guards them.

name: call_routines_with_incremented_byte
description: When an argument byte is nonzero and adding one to it does not overflow, it calls one routine, then calls two routines passing the incremented byte, followed by one more call.

description: Returns immediately for zero. Otherwise it computes an exponent from the low bits of the value, shifts the mantissa to fit, and calls several routines to process the pieces.

name: call_four_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls four other routines in sequence and returns with no other work.

name: add_or_subtract_table_entries
description: Walks a table of values for a counted number of steps, adding each entry to an accumulator while the accumulator is negative and subtracting it otherwise.

name: subtract_table_from_accumulator
description: Adds the first table entry to an accumulator, then walks the following entries, subtracting each one while the accumulator stays non-negative, until a counter runs out.

name: encode_float_with_exponent
description: Encodes a nonzero value into a float-like form using a shift-and-subtract loop of up to 22 steps, then adds an exponent by repeated doubling and calls routines to store the parts. Zero returns early.

name: encode_float_with_exponent
description: Runs the shift-and-subtract encoding loop of up to 22 steps on a value, then adds an exponent by repeated doubling and calls routines to store the result.

name: run_shift_subtract_with_exit
description: Runs a shift and subtract loop that branches on a counter and calls other routines, then adds an exponent by doubling and returns.

name: call_other_routine_thrice
description: Calls another routine three times in succession and returns.

name: store_float_parts_by_exponent
description: Handles the sign and zero cases by calling routines, then for nonzero values in range computes an exponent and shifts the mantissa, calling routines to store the parts.

name: store_float_parts_by_exponent
description: Calls two routines first, then returns for zero; otherwise it computes an exponent from the low bits, shifts the mantissa, and calls routines to store the parts.

name: call_indirect_with_offset
description: Calls a routine at an address formed by adding an offset held in an address register to a stored library base, then returns the data register value it had on entry.

name: normalize_fixed_point_value
description: Normalises a 32-bit value: a negative value is negated, a small value has its words swapped, and then it is doubled repeatedly while an exponent counts down until the top bit is set. Zero is left unchanged.

name: check_and_set_font_handle
description: Calls a library routine to obtain a handle and, if it is nonzero, stores an address argument into a field at a fixed offset before calling a second library routine. It returns whether a handle was obtained.

name: check_and_set_font_handle
description: Calls a library routine to obtain a handle and, if it is nonzero, stores an address argument into a field at a fixed offset before calling a second library routine. It returns whether a handle was obtained.

name: open_dos_and_graphics_libraries
description: Stores two register arguments in global slots, then opens the dos and graphics libraries. If both open, it sets up a list head in a new structure and returns it; on failure it closes the library and frees the block, then returns zero.

name: close_library_and_free_block
description: Closes a library and frees a memory block through the exec library, then returns zero.

name: release_idle_entries_and_unload
description: Walks a list of font records and unlinks each one whose use count has reached zero, releasing it through a library routine. If no records remain in use it closes the libraries, unloads a segment and frees the record; otherwise it sets a flag and returns zero.

name: release_record_or_flag_pending
description: If a record has no pending uses and a zero count, it closes the libraries, frees the record and returns its handle value. Otherwise it sets a pending flag in the record and returns zero.

name: set_record_pending_flag
description: Sets the pending flag with value 128 in a record byte and returns zero.

name: clear_flag_and_increment_counter
description: Clears the top bit of a flag byte in a record and increments a short counter stored at another fixed offset.

name: decrement_counter_and_release
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter in a record. When the counter reaches zero and the pending flag is set, it calls a library routine and returns its result; otherwise it returns zero.

name: scan_font_directory_entries
description: Copies names and attribute fields from a linked list of font entries into a caller buffer, and optionally scans a directory of font files to add more. It returns how far the buffer overflowed, or zero if it fitted.

name: append_font_entries_to_buffer
description: Continues copying font list entries into a buffer, writing names and attribute fields and checking a directory when a flag bit is set. It returns how far the buffer overflowed, or zero if it fitted.

name: append_font_entries_to_buffer
description: Continues copying font list entries into a buffer, writing names and attribute fields and checking a directory when a flag bit is set. It returns how far the buffer overflowed, or zero if it fitted.

name: scan_fonts_directory_into_list
description: Scans the FONTS: directory, copying each font name into a buffer and allocating list records through the exec library. It returns how far the buffer overflowed, or zero if it fitted.

name: scan_dot_font_files
description: Looks for entries whose names end in the dot-font suffix, opens each candidate through the dos library, and adds matching entries to a buffer. It returns how far the buffer overflowed, or zero if everything fitted.

name: copy_font_names_into_buffer
description: Copies font name bytes into a buffer, then reads attribute records through the dos library and adds each matching entry. It returns how far the buffer overflowed, or zero if everything fitted.

name: copy_font_names_into_buffer
description: Copies font name bytes into a buffer, then reads attribute records through the dos library and adds each matching entry. It returns how far the buffer overflowed, or zero if everything fitted.

name: read_font_records_and_release
description: Reads attribute records for font entries through the dos library, releasing locks and memory as it goes. It returns how far the buffer overflowed, or zero if everything fitted.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero and performs no other work.

name: compute_weighted_font_distance
description: Compares two font attribute records over seven flag bit positions, subtracting a weighted table value for each bit that differs, after starting from a score based on a 16-bit field difference. A missing reference record gives a fixed low score.

name: compute_font_match_score
description: Compares two font attribute records over seven flag bit positions, subtracting a weighted table value for each bit that differs, and returns the remaining score.

name: subtract_weighted_flag_differences
description: Subtracts weighted table values for each mismatched flag bit from a starting score across seven bit positions, then returns the score.

name: subtract_weighted_flag_differences
description: Subtracts weighted table values for each mismatched flag bit from a starting score across seven bit positions, then returns the score.

name: return_constant_value
description: Returns a fixed constant and uses no arguments or registers.

name: open_font_and_register
description: Opens a font through the graphics library, copies its attributes into a list entry and adds the entry to a font list. It returns the font record, or zero on failure.

name: load_font_entries_from_directory
description: Locks the FONTS: directory, reads font headers through the dos library and loads the best-scoring candidates into a list. It returns the last entry it set up.

name: load_font_entries_from_directory
description: Locks the FONTS: directory, reads font headers through the dos library and loads the best-scoring candidates into a list. It returns the last entry it set up.

name: select_best_scoring_font
description: Repeatedly picks the candidate with the highest score, loads it into a list and clears its slot until no candidate remains. It then returns the last entry set up.

name: select_best_scoring_font
description: Repeatedly picks the candidate with the highest score, loads it into a list and clears its slot until no candidate remains. It then returns the last entry set up.

name: release_font_working_records
description: Clears font slots and releases working memory, file locks and font handles through the dos, exec and graphics libraries. It returns the last entry set up.

name: release_font_working_records
description: Clears font slots and releases working memory, file locks and font handles through the dos, exec and graphics libraries. It returns the last entry set up.

name: load_font_file_header
description: Opens a font file through the dos library, checks its size and name, and allocates a memory block for its header. It returns the header pointer, or zero on failure.

name: load_disk_font_table
description: Builds a table for a disk font: it allocates a memory block, fills its header and copies entries from the source records, counting them. It returns the table pointer, or zero when nothing was loaded.

name: free_stacked_font_block
description: Reads a pointer from the caller's stack and passes it to the exec memory release routine.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from a source string to a destination until a zero byte is copied, including the terminator.

name: advance_string_end_and_call
